reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify obvious shared features across misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both pattern recognition and statistical validation of feature influence, especially for features that may appear common but lack semantic relevance to the target class.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 24699) and assess their semantic plausibility in relation to the target class (>50K).
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features across all three instances, with a note on whether they are semantically related to income class

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status, education-level) could be a spurious correlate—such as being correlated with >50K due to data leakage or sampling bias—despite lacking direct causal or logical connection to income.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned hypothesis about which shared feature is likely spurious and why

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent, interpretable feature importance scores across instances, helping identify which features drive predictions despite being semantically unrelated. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to validate attribution for each instance. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature changes the prediction, indicating spurious dependence. Together, these tools validate the autonomous findings and detect shared spurious patterns with high confidence.
